# Education in Nigeria
Education in Nigeria follows a structured system beginning with six years of primary education starting around age five, culminating in a first school-leaving certificate. The curriculum includes core subjects such as Mathematics, English, religious knowledge, agricultural science, and indigenous languages, with private schools also offering computer science, French, and fine arts. The Universal Basic Education (UBE) program mandates nine years of free, compulsory schooling—six years primary and three years junior secondary—with automatic progression assessed continuously. Secondary education lasts six years (three years junior and three years senior secondary), providing a broad curriculum and electives, and concludes with national examinations such as the Senior Secondary Certificate Examination (SSCE) conducted by bodies like the West African Examination Council (WAEC) and National Examination Council (NECO).
Federal government colleges ("unity schools") and state-sponsored schools provide most secondary education, with federal schools regarded as elite due to merit-based admission and better funding. Private and religious secondary schools offer smaller class sizes, modern facilities, and often higher-qualified teachers but can be costly. Tertiary education, comprising universities, polytechnics, and colleges of education, is predominantly government-controlled with expanding private institutions. Admission requires credits from secondary certificates and a competitive Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) exam. Vocational education is administered through national boards offering technical certificates and apprenticeship programs, although political and funding challenges affect quality and implementation. Efforts to improve female education have been bolstered by government and UNICEF projects, tackling barriers such as poverty and insecurity. Despite progress, rural education faces infrastructure deficits and teacher shortages, and literacy remains low overall, with active government initiatives targeting improvements in general and digital literacy.
